details.description: Devstral 2 123B is Mistral AI's 123-billion-parameter dense coding model, released December 9, 2025 as the larger of two Devstral 2 models (alongside a 24B 'Small' version) and the successor generation to the original Devstral. Mistral built it for agentic software-engineering work -- exploring codebases, coordinating multi-file changes, and debugging -- with tool-calling support for coding-agent frameworks such as Cline, Claude Code, OpenHands, and SWE-Agent. It supports a 256,000-token context window and is released under a modified MIT license.
advantages: Scores 72.2% on SWE-bench Verified, per Mistral's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 61.3% on SWE-bench Multilingual, per Mistral's Hugging Face model card.
Tool-calling support for agentic coding frameworks including Cline, Claude Code, OpenHands, and SWE-Agent.
disadvantages: No vision/image input mentioned for this 123B model; Mistral's smaller Devstral Small 2 (24B) supports image input instead.
Modified MIT license bars use by, or on behalf of, a company with more than $20 million in monthly revenue without a separate commercial license from Mistral.
use_cases: Agentic software-engineering tasks: codebase exploration, multi-file edits, debugging, and refactoring.
Integration with coding-agent tools via function/tool calling.
Long-context code analysis using a 256,000-token context window.

sources.title: Introducing: Devstral 2 and Mistral Vibe CLI | Mistral AI

notes: Catalog facts (256,000 max input tokens, 32,000 max output tokens, text-only modality, /v1/chat/completions endpoint) match AWS Bedrock's model card exactly. AWS Bedrock's model card lists 'Model launch date: Jun 2025' for this entry, which conflicts with Mistral's own December 9, 2025 announcement date for Devstral 2; treated Mistral's own announcement as authoritative for release date since AWS's per-model launch-date field appears to carry an incorrect/placeholder value here. Verified: the $20M/month modified-MIT revenue clause is confirmed verbatim in the model repo's own LICENSE file, and Mistral's own announcement states 'Devstral 2 is a 123B-parameter dense transformer supporting a 256K context window,' confirming both the 123B parameter count and the 'dense' architecture claim.
